thread:
maria_sales: Quick Q from ACME POC — their security team wants outbound IPs to rotate daily during the 2‑week POC and they require a CIDR allowlist. Can we support rotating egress IPs for a dedicated endpoint, or do we need to give static IPs?

liam_se: Short answer: Dedicated endpoints are easiest with static egress IPs. Rotation is possible but requires ops automation and customer coordination.

devon_eng: Two practical patterns: 1) Reserved static NAT IP(s) per customer (recommended for fast POC onboarding). 2) Ephemeral IPs behind a small published CIDR with an automated rotation/notification pipeline. Daily rotation is higher friction — doable but we need a webhook + ops runbook.

nina_security: Security note: rotation is conceptually better but often causes friction with corporate firewalls. If they insist on rotation, can we provide 24h advance notifications and signed attestations for each change? Also request: audit logs exported to customer.

liam_se: VPN or private VPC would avoid CIDR churn but is heavier and likely out of timeline for a 2‑week POC. Recommend offering static eips for the POC and a documented rotation process if they insist.

maria_sales: They insist on daily rotation for compliance reasons but said they'd accept "24h notice + automated IP list push". Can we commit to that for the POC?

devon_eng: Yes with caveats: automation needed to update NAT mapping + push notifications. There will be a short change window (~1–2 mins) while routes converge. We'll need a maintenance window in the SOW. Also need infra ticket to create the webhook and rotation job.

liam_se: Proposal to customer: provide 2 reserved EIPs per dedicated endpoint for the POC (failover), and include a documented IP rotation process: 24h notice via webhook + human ops confirmation. There will be a small infra surcharge for per‑customer reserved IPs during the POC (we'll confirm exact number).

maria_sales: They also asked about scoped API keys for dedicated endpoints (so keys only work against their POC endpoint). Can we do scoped keys?

devon_eng: Yes — we can mint API keys scoped to the dedicated endpoint + project and set expirations. Example test call: ```curl -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk-dedicated-ACME-POC-EX' https://dedicated.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"test"}'```

ops_bot: provisioner: allocated temp-reserved-eips: 35.201.12.45, 35.201.12.46 for acct ACME-POC (expires 2026-03-25T00:00:00Z).

nina_security: Confirm logging/audit: we retain request logs and can export to customer's S3 or push to their SIEM. For POC they requested 90 days retention and ACLed S3 bucket — ok?

devon_eng: We can export to an S3 bucket with IAM policy and lifecycle 90 days. Opening infra ticket INFRA-4123 to implement IP rotation webhook + S3 export + scoped key flow.

liam_se: Action items: 1) I'll update the POC SOW to request 2 reserved EIPs + 24h notice rotation process + note surcharge. 2) @devon_eng estimate hours for INFRA-4123. 3) @nina_security confirm compliance language for SOW.

maria_sales: :thumbsup: I'll send the revised SOW to ACME today and flag the 24h notice requirement. Will loop back after their firewall team responds.

liam_se: Firewall allowlist example to give customer: ```35.201.12.45/32
35.201.12.46/32```

maria_sales: Thanks all — keeping this thread for the SOW text and infra updates.
